q: A vector [4,0] points in which direction?
Can [1,0] and [2,0] span all of R²?
exp: They point in the same direction — only span a line

q: Two vectors are linearly independent if:
opts: Neither is a scalar multiple of the other
exp: Independence means you can't make one from the other by scaling
Lines stay lines, origin stays fixed

q: A 2×2 matrix represents a transformation of:
If A then B, the combined matrix is:
exp: Right-to-left: apply A first, then B, so BA
Order matters — AB ≠ BA in general

opts: Space is squished to lower dimension
exp: det=0 means the transformation collapses a dimension
Negative det = orientation reversal (like flipping a page)
Inverse undoes the transformation, returning to identity
Can't undo a transformation that squishes to lower dimension

q: If the dot product of two vectors is 0, they are:
exp: Zero dot product = 90° angle between vectors

q: An eigenvector is a vector that, after transformation:
opts: Stays on its own span (only scaled)
exp: Eigenvectors only get scaled, not knocked off their line

opts: How much the eigenvector is scaled
exp: λ is the scaling factor for that eigenvector
